study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Italinna et al., PLoS Comput Biol, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Using normative modeling and machine learning for detecting mild traumatic brain injury from magnetoencephalography data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Cam-CAN normative reference dataset (healthy participants); single-site mTBI patient/control dataset from Kaltiainen et al.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We employed a dataset originally measured by Kaltiainen and colleagues [27,28], comprising resting-state MEG recordings from 25 mild traumatic injury patients and 20 healthy controls. In addition, we employed a large, separate dataset, utilizing MEG recordings from a total of 621 healthy participants [29] as normative data."

answer.Cam-CAN: normative reference data for model construction (full dataset; also age-matched and random subsets)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Cam-CAN provides normative MEG reference used to compute mean/sd for Z-score deviations; mTBI/controls used to train/evaluate SVM classifier.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "...using MEG recordings from a total of 621 healthy participants [29] as normative data." "Three different types of normative models were constructed: a full normative model containing all participants from the reference dataset across the entire age range... age-matched models... and for comparison a random model..." "To discriminate patients from healthy control subjects, we trained support-vector-machine classifiers on the quantitative deviation maps for 25 mTBI patients and 20 controls not included in the normative dataset."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Italinna2023.pdf.md: Methods / Datasets; Methods / Fig 1; Abstract

model-3.model-name: random normative model (Cam-CAN subset matched to age-group size)
model-3.overall-phase: NR (randomly subsampled to match age-group size)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Full model uses all 621 healthy Cam-CAN subjects; age-matched model uses age-decade subsets with the listed group sizes; random model uses random-age subsets matched in size to the age-matched group.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "...MEG recordings from a total of 621 healthy participants [29] as normative data." "The number of subjects in each age group was 56, 92, 104, 93, 95, 102 and 79, from the youngest to oldest." "...the normative data used for each subject were randomly subsampled so that the size of the normative dataset was equal to the number of normative samples in the subject's age group."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Italinna2023.pdf.md: Methods / Datasets; Methods / Normative dataset; Methods / Model training and validation

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Cam-CAN normative dataset spans ages 18-87; age-matched subsets are within the defined age decades (18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57, 58-67). No mean/SD reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "...healthy participants aged 18 to 87..." "The age groups were defined according to the normative dataset as 18-27, 28-37, 38-47, 48-57 and 58-67 years."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Cam-CAN described as approximately 50 men and 50 women per age decade; exact counts not reported.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "The curated, cross-sectional Cam-CAN dataset contains measurements from approximately 50 men and 50 women in each age decade..."
